articles.title_orig: China skips Real Madrid match broadcast amid row over Mbappe's Mao joke
articles.title_zh: China skips Real Madrid match broadcast amid row over Mbappe's Mao joke
articles.content_orig:
Chinese state broadcaster CCTV did not broadcast a Real Madrid La Liga match after star forward Kylian Mbappe caused a furore in China with remarks he made about former leader Mao Zedong.
The match between Real Madrid and Racing Santander began at 1515 GMT on Sunday but was not broadcast on either of CCTV's two sports channels.
None of the other matches from the 11th round of La Liga has been broadcast live on public television so far.
A viral video in recent days showed Mbappe referring to Mao as a "dictator", prompting the body overseeing CCTV to say it would halt broadcasts of the top Spanish league.
Mbappe, Real and La Liga later all said sorry for his remarks, and China's foreign ministry said it took the player's apology "seriously".
Asked before the weekend, La Liga said that Chinese television had previously shown all games live, without specifying which platforms hosted the broadcasts.
However, reporters did find live broadcasts of matches on Migu, a digital streaming service owned by the state-owned China Mobile telecom network.
That included Barcelona's 6-1 win over Alaves on Saturday.
However, the Racing Santander–Real Madrid match did not appear to be broadcast on Sunday on Migu.
China Media Group (CMG), which oversees CCTV , had said it had moved on Monday to suspend La Liga broadcasts, adding that apologies from La Liga, Mbappe and Real Madrid were "an absolute prerequisite" for moving past the furore.
The viral video showed Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme about him he had seen was of his face photoshopped onto that of "some guy — I think he's a Chinese dictator".
This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao.
Mbappe later apologised for his "ill-judged" comments, La Liga said it "deeply" regretted them, and Real followed suit.
CCTV 's sports website later reported that CMG had acknowledged the apologies, but it remains unclear whether talks to defuse the situation have begun.
China is a huge market for European football, with CCTV also carrying matches from the Premier League as well as the German, French and Italian top flights.
Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said on Saturday that the club had "done our part" to put the controversy behind them.
Major Chinese brands cancelled sponsorship deals with Mbappe after his comments.
Various overseas sports leagues and players have found themselves in hot water for comments on topics that are politically sensitive to China.
China effectively cut ties with the NBA for several years from 2019 after then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey tweeted his support for Hong Kong protesters.

articles.title_orig: Inside Xiong'an: How China's "City of the Future" Blends Smart Governance with Sustainable Growth
articles.title_zh: Inside Xiong'an: How China's "City of the Future" Blends Smart Governance with Sustainable Growth
articles.content_orig:
Leadership to pursue ‘full and rigorous party self-governance’ with ‘not the slightest hesitation or retreat’, Xi says as fifth plenum ends
Chinese President Xi Jinping has mounted a direct defence of the campaign for strong Communist Party governance and internal discipline, describing them as a “fundamental guarantee” for China’s rise and warning against any easing of scrutiny, according to state media.
Xi took the floor as the party’s 20th Central Committee closed its fifth plenum on Thursday, to directly address the scepticism over the sweeping campaign, state news agency Xinhua reported on Sunday.
According to “side notes” released by Xinhua on a document formally approved at the end of the four-day plenary session, Xi emphasised the need to “further raise awareness of the importance and urgency of relentlessly advancing the party’s full and rigorous self-governance”.

articles.title_orig: India’s Congress Party Holds Mass Protest in New Delhi
articles.title_zh: India’s Congress Party Holds Mass Protest in New Delhi
articles.content_orig:
Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi led Sunday's protest
Tens of thousands gathered in Delhi for a rally demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner over a controversial revision of voter lists.
Organised by the opposition INDIA bloc and led by Rahul Gandhi's Congress party, the protest drew many of the alliance's most prominent leaders in a show of strength against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.
Protesters waved flags and chanted "Save the vote, save the country" and "Vote thief, give up power".
It was the latest in a series of protests over electoral roll revision that the opposition says has removed eligible voters to benefit the Bharatiya Janata Party. The BJP and the Election Commission deny the allegations.
The crowds gathered at Ramlila Maidan, a sprawling ground in central Delhi known for hosting major political and cultural events. Some protesters sang and danced to patriotic Bollywood songs, while others waited beneath a large canopy in the colours of the Indian flag to hear opposition leaders speak.
Gandhi and several senior opposition leaders arrived at the venue in an open jeep, travelling through crowds of cheering supporters.
The event was also attended by Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, alongside leaders of regional parties such as Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav, Mehbooba Mufti, Supriya Sule and Tejashwi Yadav.
Addressing the crowds, Rahul Gandhi said those gathered had sent a message to Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar .
"This is not the voice of a single political party or of politicians. It is the voice of India's youth, women, farmers and workers," he said.
"We will not allow democracy to be destroyed in India. We will not allow the constitution to be destroyed."
Other opposition leaders echoed Gandhi's criticism of the Election Commission. Congress president Kharge said the alliance would continue its campaign until Kumar resigned, while Banerjee pledged to keep fighting against what she described as threats to democracy.
Speaking to reporters in Delhi on Sunday, senior BJP leader and federal minister JP Nadda accused the opposition of trying to create unrest and destabilise the government under the guise of defending democracy.
He described the rally as a "calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy - in the name of democracy".
Tens of thousands of people gathered at the Ramlila Maidan
At the centre of the dispute is an exercise known as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which has resulted in more than 130 million names being removed from India's draft electoral rolls.
The Election Commission says the exercise is intended to remove duplicate registrations and the names of people who have died, moved away or are otherwise ineligible to vote. It says eligible voters who have been wrongly excluded can seek to have their names restored.
But opposition parties allege that the process is removing legitimate voters and could benefit the governing BJP in future elections.
The controversy deepened in September when The Indian Express newspaper reported , external that Kumar had made key decisions about the revision despite repeated objections from the two other election commissioners.
The poll panel said differences of opinion were normal in any institution and did not affect its functioning.
Sunday's rally followed weeks of protests over the voter-list revision, including demonstrations by student groups and the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).
Last month, Gandhi led tens of thousands on a march from central Delhi's Connaught Place to the Supreme Court, demanding Kumar's resignation.
The CJP also backed Sunday's rally but chose not to participate. Its founder Abhijeet Dipke said the group wanted to maintain its independence from established political parties.
People from all age groups came for the event
The event took place under strict conditions imposed by Delhi Police. According to local media reports, organisers were required to end the gathering by 5pm, install CCTV cameras at the venue and ensure that protesters did not march beyond the designated grounds.
The restrictions came against a backdrop of tensions over the policing of demonstrations in the capital. On 10 October , several leaders of the CJP were detained during protests against Kumar, while BBC reporters witnessed police dragging demonstrators away and beating some with batons.
At Ramlila Maidan, however, the atmosphere was largely peaceful, with people of different ages and professions turning out to express their concerns about the integrity of India's elections.
"We don't even know if this is a people's mandate or a stolen mandate," Isha, a development sector professional from Delhi, told the BBC.
Deepro Guha, a lawyer from Delhi, said he was concerned about the way the revision had been carried out.
"It's important because voting is the basis of democracy. If people's names are removed without any explanation, there is a problem," he said.
Opposition alliance held a mock impeachment of CEC Kumar on Saturday
On Saturday, opposition leaders also staged a symbolic impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of undermining the electoral process.
The proceedings were purely symbolic and had no legal standing. Under Indian law, the chief election commissioner can only be removed through a formal parliamentary process.
But the move was another show of unity by the INDIA bloc, an alliance of opposition parties formed in 2023 to to take on Modi's BJP.
Modi did not directly comment on the mock impeachment, but at public rallies on Friday and Saturday he accused opposition parties of trying to create chaos and undermining the dignity of the constitution.

articles.title_orig: China’s Communist Party Tightens Internal Discipline, Demands Unwavering Loyalty
articles.title_zh: China’s Communist Party Tightens Internal Discipline, Demands Unwavering Loyalty
articles.content_orig:
China's ruling Communist Party emphasized loyalty in a new resolution aimed at strengthening internal discipline and continuing its anti-corruption efforts.
China’s ruling Communist Party emphasized loyalty in a new resolution aimed at strengthening internal discipline and continuing its anti-corruption efforts. This resolution, discussed at a recent party leadership meeting, calls for enhancing loyalty among members and judging officials based on their commitment to party values, as seen through their work, behavior, and family values.
The resolution acknowledges ongoing problems such as ideological and organizational impurities and aims to address them through an extensive anti-graft campaign that has already affected millions in the bureaucracy. This initiative comes in anticipation of a leadership change where President Xi Jinping is expected to secure another five-year term.
The party plans to improve oversight of officials, including stricter checks on personal disclosures and the financial activities of their families. The anti-corruption campaign will also target hidden forms of graft, including the misuse of technology and financial systems to facilitate corruption.
While promoting collective leadership, the document still reinforces Xi’s authority, urging party members to support him fully in thought and action. Xi emphasized the importance of rigorous self-governance to maintain the party’s integrity and legacy for future generations.

articles.title_orig: At 75, the IRS Will Set the Withdrawal Amount on a $900,000 401(k). Affluent Investors Over 60 Are Making Sure It's Empty by Then - 24/7 Wall St.
articles.title_zh: At 75, the IRS Will Set the Withdrawal Amount on a $900,000 401(k). Affluent Investors Over 60 Are Making Sure It's Empty by Then - 24/7 Wall St.
articles.content_orig:
The IRS gets to decide how much comes out of your 401(k) at 75, and the tax cascade that follows can push your effective marginal rate past 40 percent. There is a narrow window before that clock runs out, and…
The Full Benefits Desk desk. Editor: Gerelyn Terzo .
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
Picture a 62-year-old with $900,000 in a traditional 401(k) and a retirement date coming up soon. He doesn’t want the IRS setting his withdrawals later. If he leaves the account alone, the IRS starts making that call at 75.
Many people are working through the same problem. On Reddit, a 54-year-old with $720,000 in a 401(k) was told, “You’ll probably do a more substantial amount after 65 once you’re on Medicare.” That timing can be expensive.
Under current law, the required minimum distribution (RMD) starting age is 75 for anyone who turns 74 after December 31, 2032. Our 62-year-old was born in 1964, so that rule covers him. If he skips a required withdrawal, he can face a 25% excise tax, falling to 10% if corrected in time.
Roth IRAs get different treatment. The original owner never has to take required minimum distributions while alive. Every dollar that moves to a Roth before 75 is a dollar the IRS can’t force out later.
Assume 5% annual returns and 13 years until age 75. To empty the account by then, he needs to take out about $91,250 at the start of each year.
If he leaves it untouched, the same $900,000 grows to roughly $1.7 million by 75.
The IRS Uniform Lifetime Table divisor at that age is 24.6, so his first RMD comes to about $69,000.
By 85 the divisor drops to 16.0, which increases the required share of the balance from about 4% to over 6% a year.
Say he files jointly and the withdrawal is the couple’s only taxable income early in retirement. The 2026 standard deduction of $32,200 leaves $59,050 of taxable income.
All of it lands in the 10% and 12% brackets, and the 12% bracket runs up to $100,800.
The federal bill is about $6,590, an effective rate near 7%. Whatever part he doesn’t need to live on can instead move directly into a Roth IRA through a taxable rollover. Emptying the pretax account and spending the money are two separate decisions. That converted money can keep growing, with qualified withdrawals tax-free.
Now picture the untouched account at 75, with RMDs stacked on top of Social Security. On a joint return, benefits start becoming taxable once combined income passes $32,000, and the second threshold is $44,000. Up to 85% of benefits can end up taxable.
In that phase-in range, each extra RMD dollar taxed at 22% draws 85 cents of benefits into taxable income along with it. That works out to an effective marginal rate of about 41%.
After the year one spouse dies, the survivor generally files single. Under 2026 rules, the first Medicare surcharge threshold falls from $218,000 to $109,000.
Medicare’s income-related monthly adjustment amount (IRMAA) generally uses income from two years earlier. A conversion at 62 ordinarily won’t affect his Medicare premiums at 65. From 63 on, conversions can affect future premiums. That makes 62 an attractive window, although health insurance costs before Medicare matter too.
Under 2026 rules, a $91,250 conversion alone sits below the joint threshold of $218,000. Add a large capital gain on top and the couple could cross it.
The first level adds $81.20 a month per person to the standard $202.90 Part B premium , plus $14.50 for Part D.
For a married couple who can convert at around 7% now instead of facing a possible 41% marginal rate later, emptying the 401(k) on their own schedule comes out ahead.

A veteran financial journalist, she covers agri-finance for outlets like Global AgInvesting and the broader stock market and personal finance for 24/7 Wall Street. She began at CNBC and later helped launch Fox Business in New York. Gerelyn currently resides in Woodland Park, Colorado and dabbles in nature photography as a hobby.

articles.title_orig: Israel election: When will government be formed, who will lead it?
articles.title_zh: Israel election: When will government be formed, who will lead it?
articles.content_orig:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has lost his coalition’s parliamentary majority following legislative elections on October 27.
But a bloc of Jewish parties opposing Netanyahu also failed to win a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, leaving Israel without a clear path to a new government.
What’s ahead is likely weeks of political wrangling as Israel’s disparate factions weigh possible governing arrangements, including a unity government bringing rival factions together or a minority government reliant on outside support. If they fail to reach an agreement, Israel could head back to the polls.
Here’s what you should know:
The pro-Netanyahu coalition won 53 seats:
A bloc of Jewish parties opposing Netanyahu won 48 seats:
Arab-led parties won 19 seats:
That leaves all existing blocs short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset, meaning some parties would have to realign or join forces across bloc lines to form a new government.
Israel’s election results must be officially certified and presented to President Isaac Herzog by November 4 .
The new Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10 .
Herzog must task one incoming Knesset member with forming a new government by November 11 . He is expected to make his decision with input from party leaders, selecting the candidate he believes has the best chance of building a coalition.
The candidate commissioned by Herzog has 28 days to form a coalition, with a possible extension of 14 days .
He has not said yet, but the most likely candidates are Netanyahu or former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, whose Yashar party received the most votes in the opposition bloc.
According to Israel’s Yedioth Ahronoth media, Eisenkot may have an edge over Netanyahu as some Arab-led parties consider endorsing him in a bid to oust Netanyahu.
Herzog, for his part, has urged Israeli politicians to move away from rigid partisan stances and look for “creative solutions” that will lead to a new government and avoid a second round of elections.
Before the election, Herzog said he would do everything he could to spare the country another election cycle, even if that means pressing for a national unity government that brings together rivals Netanyahu and Eisenkot.
Eisenkot and other opposition leaders have previously ruled out partnering with the Arab-led parties .
Former Prime Minister Ehud Barak, however, has said he believes they “can change their mind”, arguing that Netanyahu would do in their position.
“If Netanyahu had a similar problem, he would immediately invite Mansour Abbas”, the leader of Ra’am and “give him the role of a minister of interior”, Barak told France 24 on Friday.
Abbas himself has signalled a willingness to work the opposition camp, saying Eisenkot’s conditions would not pose an obstacle for his party, according to Israel’s Channel 12.
Yousef Jabareen from the Arab-led Joint List has also said that his party is ready for the “ousting of the Netanyahu government”.
“The change comes through Jewish-Arab partnership, a true and equal partnership,” he wrote on X.
Even if Arab-led parties do not formally join the opposition’s coalition, they could prop it up from outside by helping it pass a confidence vote in the Knesset.
Raluca Ganea, co-founder of Israeli civil society group Zazim, told Al Jazeera that a coalition between the opposition bloc and the Arab-led parties representing the Palestinian citizens of Israel “is the only path forward for Israeli democracy as a whole”.
If Herzog’s first candidate fails to form a government within the 42 days, the Israeli president has the option of asking another Knesset member to try to do so within 28 days. If that candidate also fails, a majority of Knesset members could put forward a third candidate, who would have a final 14 days to try to assemble one.
Even without a coalition commanding at least 61 seats, a candidate could still try to form a minority government by relying on outside support from smaller parties, including Arab-led parties, or negotiate a power-sharing arrangement with alternating prime ministers.
If none of these options succeed and deadlock persists, the Knesset would be formally dissolved, and Israelis would return to the polls for another round of elections.
Those elections would have to be called within 90 days.
Netanyahu stays on as caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed.
If the process drags out, that could leave Israel’s longest-serving prime minister in power for months more, even if he ultimately fails to become part of the next governing coalition.

articles.title_orig: King to address slavery during Commonwealth speech in Antigua on final leg of Caribbean tour
articles.title_zh: King to address slavery during Commonwealth speech in Antigua on final leg of Caribbean tour
articles.content_orig:
King Charles III is to speak with "unflinching honesty" and "sincere sorrow" on the lasting pain of the transatlantic slave trade, during the final leg of his Caribbean tour in Antigua, Buckingham Palace has said.
The King will address Commonwealth leaders on Tuesday in a speech which will touch on the issue.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier he was "open" to the possibility of the UK formally apologising for its role in slavery - a change in the government's stance.
It is understood the Palace was told in advance of Burnham's comments in an opinion piece on Friday night, and the King has not made any changes to his speech in light of them.
The British government has never formally apologised for slavery or offered to pay reparations.
Burnham has previously stuck with the policy of his predecessors, and stopped short of offering any consideration of reparation payments.
Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch described "endless talk about apologies" as a "distraction" from solving current problems.
She told BBC Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "The transatlantic slave trade happened centuries ago. It is time for the Commonwealth to start looking forwards, not endlessly backwards."
The King will make his speech at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM).
He "will not shy away from confronting the most shameful aspects of the past during this visit", a Palace spokesperson said.
"You may therefore expect him to address them in his speech with unflinching honesty, sincere sorrow, and respect for the wider discussions that will be taking place between relevant governments on this issue at CHOGM and beyond."
When asked about the King's reaction to the prime minister's comments, the spokesperson said it would "not be appropriate" for the King to address matters of policy relating to "the UK government's position".
The Caribbean tour has again thrust King Charles into the difficult debates over the UK's colonial legacy in the region.
On his first stop in the Bahamas, the King delivered a speech where he spoke of the "suffering of the past".
In Guyana, he visited the site of a Slave Rebellion where hundreds of enslaved people were killed.
Buckingham Palace said it was a moment for the King to learn more about the history of slavery and resistance. His engagements have also covered the environment, opportunities for young people and trade relationships with the UK.
Royal sources have stressed that the decisions around making an apology are a matter for government, not the Palace.
"His Majesty is well practised on the diplomatic tightrope," a Royal aide said. "He is up for challenging visits with complex issues and relationships in play. He sees it as his role to 'bat for Britain', the Realms and wider Commonwealth."
In a piece for the Guardian published on Friday night, Burnham described the transatlantic slave trade as a "brutal and barbaric violation" , and that Britain "must face up to the past".
His pledge to strengthen the work of the Commonwealth as an organisation will be welcomed by King Charles, who views the collection of 56 countries as a powerful vehicle for change.
"Institutions are under strain across the globe," said a Palace spokesperson. "The Commonwealth has scale and breadth, but is also small enough for leaders to know each other and co-operate together."
The King, they said, "contributes ideas and encouragement on a wide range of issues, delivering practical results which help improve the lives of millions".
Queen Camilla is with the King in Antigua, they have attended a church service on Sunday morning ahead of joining celebrations to mark Independence Day on the island.
It has been a difficult few months for the King, with developments surrounding his brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor , and the publication of a book by his former brother-in-law, Earl Spencer.
In addition, his son the Duke of Sussex made a surprise move back to the UK with his wife Meghan and their two children in August.
Asked if the King was confident that his approach to family matters had been the right one in terms of public attitudes towards the institution, the response was concise. "Yes," a senior aide told the BBC. "That is why he takes the actions he does - and has done."
On the serious allegations that have emerged about Meghan's father , Thomas Markle, the Palace did not want to get involved publicly: "We wouldn't comment on private family matters."
The King is also still being treated for cancer. He was diagnosed in early 2024 and the Palace says he remains on a "positive trajectory".
In hot and humid conditions, he will soon celebrate his 78th birthday and will have carried out about 36 engagements by the end of this nine-day tour of the Caribbean.

The holiday season is hurtling toward us like a freight train, and there's nothing we can do about it — except maybe allow ourselves some retail therapy at Costco, the store that has it all (and in bulk quantities). The wholesale retailer has lots of great new finds for November, so we're highlighting some highly rated items. This month, you'll find cookware, gourmet chocolates, energy drinks, holiday glassware, snacks, and more.
Something to keep in mind about Costco: The store's online inventory and in-store stock aren't always the same. As such, some of these November finds are only available for purchase online. But don't worry — we included links to each product.
You may also notice that our selection is mostly name-brand products, with just one Kirkland Signature item in the mix. While Costco's store brand is beloved for its quality and affordability, the chain stocks a wide selection of name-brand items to ensure members have lots to choose from. Speaking of impressive Kirkland Signature products, here's how Costco's pumpkin pie compares to the one from Sam's Club in terms of tastiness and overall value (after all, it's never too early to start planning your Thanksgiving menu).
This versatile, induction-compatible cookware is great for braising, searing, roasting, and baking. As one Costco member put it in their review, "This braising pan is high quality and even better than I expected. It's my go to pan already for dinner."
You can buy this Tramontina 4-Quart Enameled Cast Iron Covered Braiser online for $58.99.
This gourmet shortbread set comes with 24 individual boxes, which equals 96 cookies in total. That makes them perfect for random gift giving. "I'm going to give out [these cookies] during the holidays to neighbors etc.," wrote a reviewer on the Costco site.

If you love crispy snacks but are burned out on chips and pretzels, rice crackers are the next logical step. Dubbed "Best snack crackers ever" by a Costco reviewer, the shopper described them as "Spicy, salty sweet and crunchy you can't do much better." Each 2-pound bag comes with varieties like Chili Mochi, Sesame Half Moon, Wasabi Crescent, and plenty more.
You can buy these Kirkland Signature Rice Crackers online for $12.49.
If you know any chocolate snobs who hold the European view that Hershey's is gross (thanks to one infamous flavor note), Costco has the perfect gift. This 2-pound pack comes with 100 individual pieces in milk, white, and dark chocolate.
You can buy this Hebert Candies Heritage Chocolate Assortment online for $59.99.
This mushroom-infused coffee is a good example of at least one of the food trends that swept through 2026 . Featuring a blend of mushrooms intended to support immune function, reduce stress, and improve concentration, the convenient brew received accolades from Costco reviewers, with one writing, "Portable, delicious and good for you and your brain!"
You can buy 60 servings of Wunderground Craft Instant Coffee Plus Mushroom online for $59.99.
"Very worth the price," wrote a Costco shopper about this cute holiday glassware set. You get four glasses with different seasonally inspired designs. They're also very sturdily made; as another reviewer noted, "The design does not sit on the glass but also feels like a small glass object embossed in the glass."
You can buy this four-piece Pandex Holiday Icon Glasses Set online for $29.99.
According to a review on the Costco website, this holiday-inspired soda is "Really good and taste[s] like a frosted cranberry." Along with seasonal varieties, the soda brand offers lots of regular flavors as well. Here's our ranking of every Poppi flavor from worst to best to whet your whistle.

Of all the popular ways to pop popcorn , a stovetop popper offers a one-way ticket to nostalgia town. (Did we mention that it's also among the tastiest methods?) With a 4.4-star member rating as of this writing, this GreenPan popper is currently $12 off its regular price and is compatible with gas, electric, and induction cooktops.
You can buy this GreenPan 5.39 qt. Stainless Steel Popcorn Popper online for $45.99 (price valid through November 22).
Here's the awesome thing about gift bundles like this one from Ethel M Chocolates: There's nothing stopping you from keeping one box for yourself and enjoying rich, decadent flavors like Maple Walnut Satin Crème and Macadamia Salute. "Delish," wrote a Costco reviewer of these gourmet chocolates.
You can buy this Ethel M Chocolates Nuts and Caramels Collection Bundle online for $59.99.
While it doesn't rank among the best-selling energy drinks in the U.S. , Ghost is pretty popular in its own right. In the words of one Costco shopper, "Best energy drinks out there. I don't experience any crash, the flavors are phenomenal, and you can't beat the price!!!" This vibe-licious variety pack includes 18 total beverages and comes in Welch's Grape-Cran, Blue Raspberry, and Strawbango flavors.

articles.title_orig: Samsung joins cuff-shaped earbuds trend with $229 Galaxy Buds On
articles.title_zh: Samsung joins cuff-shaped earbuds trend with $229 Galaxy Buds On
articles.content_orig:
It's got a clip-on design to keep them in place.
As competitors like Sony, Bose and Sennheiser reveal their takes on open-ear wireless earbuds, Samsung is taking another stab with the Galaxy Buds On, featuring a clip-on design for a more secure fit. While they don't pack high-level noise cancellation like the Galaxy Buds 4 Pro, the company claims its new Audio Leakage Reduction tech reduces sound leakage by protecting reversed sound waves at the rear of each bud, ostensibly canceling it out. The company says it pulled data from over 119 million ear scans to help the Buds On fit across a range of ear shapes and sizes and have IP54 water resistance.
They're also designed to ensure a low-pressure fit around the ear, something many of us crave from open-ear buds, avoiding the discomfort from typical wireless headphones that form a seal around the ear canal. As mentioned, these aren't Samsung's first open-type design; you might recall the underwhelming Galaxy Buds Live . The more recent (and better) Galaxy Buds 4 launched earlier this year and also have an open-type, semi-in-ear profile like recent AirPods.
The Galaxy Buds On pack a new high-efficiency Class-D amplifier designed to balance power consumption and punchy sound. Battery life also looks solid, with an estimated 9.5 hours of music playback on a single charge. With the charging case, that should stretch to 38 hours.
Samsung's newest buds pack three mics and a voice pickup unit (VPU) that detects speech vibrations, which work together to isolate the caller's voice and cut out noise. Algorithms have been trained on a range of ambient sounds, including construction noises and car horns (is that a regular occurrence on your calls?). The Buds On also pack in head-gesture controls: nod or shake your head to accept or decline calls, and even dismiss alarms and notification readouts. The buds will also work with Galaxy smartphone features, including access to Gemini Live, Quick Voice Memo recordings and will connect to Galaxy phones as soon as you open the case.
The Galaxy Buds On will launch in early November 2026 and will be priced at $229.

articles.title_orig: HomePod Mini 2 first look: Three things I love and one disappointment
articles.title_zh: HomePod Mini 2 first look: Three things I love and one disappointment
articles.content_orig:
The new Mini is faster, quieter, and gorgeous in green, but its upgraded Mac speaker feature didn’t work for me.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
When I first heard about the new $149 HomePod Mini 2 at Apple’s Welcome Home event last month, I was disappointed. It’s been six years since Apple launched its entry-level smart speaker, and all it got in the second gen was a chip bump, some color glowy stuff, and better AirPlay? For $50 more than the original, which launched at $99, Apple didn’t even upgrade the sound system. It felt like the company phoned this one in.
Now that I’ve got my hands on a couple and set them up in my home office, I’m more enthused. The Mini 2 is so much faster than the first-gen Mini, playing music in a few seconds and responding to smart home commands just as quickly. If you’re fed up with standing over your HomePod waiting for it to finally do what you asked, then that alone is worth the upgrade.
Here are my three favorite features of the new Mini 2 after spending a couple days with it, and my one big disappointment.
The biggest upgrade for the Mini 2 is Siri AI , but that isn’t available yet. Apple says it’s coming “later” in a software update. However, the basic smart voice assistant has definitely improved. Siri on the Mini 2 is much snappier than on the first-gen Mini, regularly responding in under three seconds. This is thanks to a newer, faster processor (the S10, up from the S5) and Wi-Fi 6E support (up from Wi-Fi 4).
When I asked Siri to play Taylor Swift, a song started in a couple of seconds. It correctly told me who won this year’s World Series in under two seconds, and turned off the light or opened the shades in under three seconds.
That’s a huge improvement over the up to 10 seconds I often have to wait for Siri to get things done on the first-gen Mini. However, asking something harder, like who will win the US midterm elections, still brings up the familiar offer to look at some web results on my iPhone. As I said, Siri AI isn’t here yet.
The other new behavior I am really enjoying is that when I ask Siri to perform a smart home action, such as open the shades or turn on the lights, instead of “OK, Jen,” or “One sec,” followed by a wordy confirmation of the action that I often get on the first-gen Mini, the Mini 2 just does it and doesn’t talk back. It’s not silent for every action, but it’s quiet enough to be a noticeable improvement.
The green color is divine. This is the prettiest small smart speaker I’ve seen — and I’ve tried them all.
Yes, Amazon’s Echo Dot Max’s purple is fun , the Google Home Speaker’s pale green is elegant , but Apple’s deep green is seriously sophisticated. It’s a color that fits in really well in various places around my home, and I’m so glad the company finally released a green option. It’s a big improvement over the slightly garish yellow and orange of the prior-gen Minis and the best of the new colors.
I saw all the colors in person at Apple’s Welcome Home event , and while the pink is pretty, it’s very pale, and the blue is functionally identical to the first-gen blue, maybe a shade lighter. While a lot of folks will be happy with black (don’t get white unless you plan to dust it regularly), the green is my new go-to.
Two green HomePod Mini 2s look so good on the walnut Nanoleaf monitor stand I’m testing ; it’s like my office got an instant upgrade. And while Apple didn’t update the speakers in the Mini 2, it’s still a very good speaker for its size, doing a fine job with Bad Bunny’s bass and delivering clear mids and vocals. While $300 is steep for computer speakers, two as a stereo pair in my office definitely delivered on room-filling sound.
A few weeks ago I fumbled for my phone on my nightstand and accidentally hit the top of my HomePod Mini, blaring music in the bedroom at 3AM. My husband was not happy.
A new setting in the Home app now lets you lock the Mini’s top controls. This goes for all HomePods, old and new, and it’s a major quality-of-life upgrade. How often do you intentionally touch the top of your HomePod? I bet far less often than accidentally!
The other new trick for the top of the HomePod is Sound Glow. This makes the LEDs display colors that match the album art of the song you’re playing (it’s also backward compatible with the first-gen Mini and the second-gen HomePod). It’s neat, but only works with Apple Music and Podcasts and is so subtle that I don’t feel it adds much to my music-listening experience.
Beyond the speed improvement, the other new feature I was excited about is the HomePod Mini 2’s ability to be the default speaker for your Mac using what Apple calls “a responsive and persistent AirPlay connection.” This creates a wireless point-to-point connection between the computer and the HomePod.
You can pair a single speaker or a stereo pair to your Mac, and the feature also works with the second-gen HomePod. (Two or four HomePod Mini 2s can also now be part of a surround sound setup using the new Apple TV 4K.)
Disappointingly, I couldn’t get the Mac speaker set up to work. I have the required hardware: a Mac that supports Wi-Fi 6E, running the public release of macOS 27.2 (a Mac Mini M4), and HomePods on HomePod Software 27.2 . But the Sound pane in my Mac’s settings didn’t offer an option to set a HomePod via AirPlay as the default sound output.
The Mini showed up and connected like any other AirPlay speaker, with the same flaws as regular AirPlay — occasional artifacting, drop-offs, and some lag with notification sounds — along with the Mac defaulting to its built-in speakers when the computer restarts, or anytime I activate Siri on the HomePod. I also tried with a stereo pair of Minis, but they also played over regular AirPlay.
The chip bump and speed improvements make this a bigger upgrade than it initially seemed
According to a 9to5Mac’s hands-on , when the persistent AirPlay is enabled, the HomePod Mini should show up as a default system output device in the System Information, and there should be an option to enable it under “Play sound effects through” in the Sound pane in System Settings, but neither was there for me. I have seen other reports of the same issue.
I tried resetting both HomePods completely after they updated to 27.2 out of the box (I was on the HomePod Software betas, but 27.2 is now in general release), and the feature still isn’t working. I reached out to Apple, but the company hasn’t responded to my requests yet; I’ll update this article if I hear back or find a solution.
I’ve only been testing the Mini 2 for two days, and while the real test will come when it gets its Siri AI upgrade, the chip bump and speed improvements make this a bigger upgrade than it initially seemed. Apple does need to work on the Mac pairing feature; it has a lot of potential, but based on my struggles here, it feels unfinished.
I plan to do a full review once Siri AI launches, and of course compare it to Apple’s big new smart home release: the upcoming $299 Apple HomeView smart display. It is also a Home hub, but the screen gives it more functionality. At $149, though, the Mini 2 is now the cheapest way to get an Apple Home hub with Thread and Matter support.

articles.title_orig: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy
articles.title_zh: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy
articles.content_orig:
More than 300 people have been arrested during a protest supporting the banned Palestine Action group outside the US embassy, police have said.
Hundreds of people gathered at Nine Elms in London on Saturday, with many holding signs reading phrases such as: "I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action."
The Metropolitan Police said on Sunday that 325 arrests were made. The force added on social media that 320 of them were for "expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act".
At least 4,000 arrests have been made in relation to the group, which was proscribed in July 2025.
The UK Supreme Court is due to review Palestine Action's ban under terrorism legislation , after the group's co-founder was granted permission to appeal it.
The Home Office has said that it will robustly defend against the appeal.
Officers on Saturday made arrests into the evening, taking people to police vans for transfer, to the applause of many protesters, some of whom chanted: "Free, free Palestine."
In some instances, officers had to carry demonstrators who refused to walk.
Retired lawyer Charles Allison - who was taken by police in the afternoon  - had travelled from Cumbria to participate. He said he feared for people's civil liberties, which he said were "being devalued and watered down".
"I hope the Supreme Court justices - they won't necessarily be influenced by it [the protest] - but I hope that they will take a long-term view of what is happening in this country and decide that the proscription was unlawful, as I believe it was," the 75-year-old said.
David Bolden, another protester awaiting arrest called the ban an "absurd law".
Defend Our Juries, which has been co-ordinating a series of protests over the ban, said the number of people detained this weekend took the total over 4,000 arrests since the group was proscribed, calling it "truly dystopian".
According to Home Office figures seen by the BBC, 3,630 arrests were made in the year ending June 2026. Along with the 134 people arrested outside Westminster Magistrates Court earlier this year and those on Saturday brings the total up to 4,089.
The BBC has contacted the Met to confirm any figures it might hold.
Amnesty International UK has criticised the arrests and called for the government to drop the proscription of Palestine Action.
Defend Our Juries called the arrests "unjust" and an assault on free speech.

articles.title_orig: I imported a $2,000 electric truck from China. Five years later, here’s the truth
articles.title_zh: I imported a $2,000 electric truck from China. Five years later, here’s the truth
articles.content_orig:
Five years ago, I did something that seemed pretty ridiculous at the time. I bought a $2,000 electric mini-truck from China, had it shipped across the oceans to the US, and put it to work on my parents’ property in Florida.
The little white mini electric truck became something of an internet sensation, with my original unboxing and testing video quickly racking up over 10 million views, plus several million more from the follow-up videos.
It also attracted plenty of skeptics who were convinced that a $2,000 Chinese electric truck would fall apart within months, rust into oblivion, or otherwise prove to be a spectacular waste of money. “Good thing it has a bed,” was a common refrain. “So you can collect all the pieces that fall off along the way.”
I gave an update after the first year , showing that the truck was doing great. But to be fair, one year doesn’t tell us much.
Well now it’s been over five years, and I recently returned to Florida to see how the little truck has held up after five trips around the sun on my parents’ homestead. And I’ve got to say, the results are pretty surprising.
So here’s the truth about how the truck is doing five years later. Oh, and if you want to see it in action, you can check out my update video here . Trust me, you’ll want to.
First, it’s important to understand that this truck hasn’t spent five years sitting in a garage as some kind of novelty vehicle. It’s been a genuine workhorse on my parents’ 10-acre homestead.
Over the years, we’ve used it to haul everything from mulch and sand to lumber, tree branches, logs, yard waste, and everything in between.
Its hydraulic dump bed makes it particularly useful for moving bulk materials around the property, like hauling mulch and then dumping it in their raised planting beds.
My dad even uses it as a mobile irrigation truck during Florida’s dry season. I built him a solar-powered pump system that fills a water bladder in the truck’s bed with water from his pond, allowing him to drive around watering his trees and plants.
By now, it’s been involved in practically every major landscaping and construction project my parents have tackled.
We’ve also made some improvements over the years. Early on, my dad and I replaced the ridiculously stiff factory suspension springs with softer ones, making the ride considerably more comfortable. We added a custom tow hitch and swapped the original street tires for aggressive off-road tires that work much better on the property’s sandy and muddy terrain.
The suspension upgrade did reduce how much weight we can comfortably carry, though. Load more than around 500 pounds (220 kg) of sand or other bulk materials into the bed, and the rear end starts squatting enough that our homemade tow hitch threatens to touch grass.
But for most of the work we do, it’s been an excellent little utility vehicle.
And before anyone asks, no, this isn’t a street-legal truck. It was never really designed for American roads, and we use it almost exclusively on private property. Sure, it’s hit the pavement a few times since they live out in the boonies and its normal to see tractors and other non-street-legal vehicles on country roads, but it’s not the most ideal vehicle for long distance transport at 25 mph (40 km/h).
Here’s the part that surprised me most: Almost everything still works.
The electric windows still zip up and down with the speed of a guillotine. The electric door locks work. The headlights work. The backup camera works. Even the air conditioning still blows impressively cold air.
I actually checked that last one with a thermal camera during my latest visit, and the air coming out of the vents was around 55°F (12°C). Not bad for a five-year-old air conditioning system in a $2,000 truck!
Of course, not everything is perfect.
The windshield wiper still operates, but its range of motion has decreased significantly. It now stops around the middle of the driver’s field of vision, which isn’t ideal when Florida’s famous afternoon thunderstorms roll through.
The rearview mirror has also developed an annoying habit of falling off. We’ve glued it back on multiple times, and it looks like another round of adhesive surgery is coming soon.
Inside, there’s some minor upholstery damage on the driver’s seat, including a few small tears and stressed seams in the cheap faux-leather material that you can see in the video .
The passenger seat, which sees much less use, still looks nearly new. In another few years, I might just swap the two seats to get another half decade or so out of them before we need some upholstery repair.
One decorative plastic panel around the driver’s door handle has popped off, though I still have the piece and could probably snap it back into place with a bit of effort. It’s just aesthetic though, so it’s been a low-priority repair.
And that’s pretty much the extent of the mechanical and electrical problems we’ve encountered.
There haven’t been any major drivetrain failures, the hydraulic dump bed still works, and the truck continues to start up and drive just as reliably as it did when it was new.
It still gets used for lots of bulk jobs, material hauling, and sometimes just random transportation around the property.
One of the biggest predictions from critics five years ago was that this cheap Chinese truck would quickly dissolve into a pile of rust.
To be fair, there is some rust. But nowhere near as much as you might expect.
Most of the corrosion is concentrated in areas where the paint has been scratched or chipped, especially around the tailgate and cargo bed.
The rustiest spot is definitely the top lip of the tailgate, where we usually have long objects hanging out of the bed, such as shovels, ladders, lumber, etc. The paint has worn through on that edge, and the rust has inevitably started in those few spots.
The truck is stored outdoors under a lean-to roof that I built between two shipping containers, but we have a skid-steer in front of it and so the rear of the truck sticks out and gets rained on several times a week (or several times a day during the summer).
We applied a paint-on bed liner during the truck’s first year, which helped protect the metal for quite a while.
After four years of hauling dirt, rocks, branches, and other abrasive materials though, that coating has started wearing through in a few places.
Every time I’m shoveling mulch out of the bed and I hear that scrape of metal on metal, I cringe just a bit before remembering that the truck cost me $2,000 and doesn’t owe me anything at this point.
Speaking of being parked outdoors with the rear hanging out for the world (and the UV) to see, there’s clearly an effect on the truck’s wear.
You can absolutely see the difference in the paint and plastic components. The front headlight lenses are still crystal clear, while the rear taillight lenses have become noticeably cloudy from UV exposure.
Despite that, the truck’s basic structure remains solid, and the rust is mostly cosmetic and limited to the high-impact areas that tend to get beaten up repeatedly, as you’d expect in any self-respecting work truck.
Considering that Florida combines high humidity, frequent rain, and intense sunshine, I’d call that a pretty impressive result for a vehicle that cost less than many electric bicycles.
Since the truck lives at my parents’ property, my dad has actually spent far more time using it than I have.
And when I asked him how he felt about the purchase after five years, he was surprisingly enthusiastic.
He described the truck as an incredibly functional piece of equipment that has become an essential part of maintaining the property.
In fact, he pointed out that the truck has been involved in virtually every significant project they’ve completed over the past five years.
It isn’t the only electric utility vehicle on the property anymore. My parents also have a Kandi electric UTV , which has taken over some of the smaller daily chores thanks to its better suspension and more c

articles.title_orig: Ukraine Liberated 96 Sq Km in October, Inflicted Record Losses
articles.title_zh: Ukraine Liberated 96 Sq Km in October, Inflicted Record Losses
articles.content_orig:
In brief: Ukrainian Defense Forces liberated 96.2 square kilometers of sovereign territory in October – surpassing Russian territorial advances by 10.4 square kilometers – while inflicting a record 54,400 casualties on the Russian military, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sunday, Nov. 1. Calling the milestone the highest monthly toll of the full-scale war, Zelensky noted that Russian daily casualties peaked at 2,250 on Oct. 21. The president also commended all combat units for holding lines, recovering land, and maximizing the war’s cost to the aggressor, emphasizing that Moscow need only choose an immediate ceasefire and diplomacy to halt its losses.
The Defense Forces of Ukraine liberated 96.2 square kilometers of sovereign territory in October – surpassing Russian territorial advances by 10.4 square kilometers – while inflicting an unprecedented 54,400 casualties on the Russian military, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sunday, Nov. 1.
Writing on Telegram , the head of state presented a monthly assessment establishing that Ukrainian forces recaptured more land than Russian occupying units seized over the same 31-day period, while extracting the highest monthly casualty toll recorded since the beginning of the full-scale invasion in February 2022 .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“In October, our Defense Forces of Ukraine inflicted record losses on the enemy and regained more territory than the Russian occupiers were able to capture,” Zelensky stated.
According to data presented by the president, Russian forces suffered 54,400 military personnel killed and severely wounded during the month. The monthly attrition rate also produced a single-day casualty record on Oct. 21, when Russian forces sustained 2,250 casualties within a single 24-hour cycle.
“It is important that we continue to take back what is ours,” Zelensky emphasized.
“During October, the Defense Forces liberated 96.2 square kilometers of Ukrainian land, which is 10.4 square kilometers more than the occupiers managed to capture during this time.”
The president extended formal commendations to all Ukrainian soldiers, combat brigades, and specialized service branches contributing to the counter-offensive maneuvers and frontline containment operations.
“Russia is losing. We are holding positions, liberating territory, and ensuring that every day of the war costs the aggressor as dearly as possible,” Zelensky underscored, adding that to halt these severe losses, Moscow need only choose an immediate ceasefire and genuine diplomacy.
A decisive component of Ukraine’s battlefield efficiency in October stemmed from the operational scale of the Unmanned Systems Forces (USF).
Earlier on Sunday, USF Commander Robert “Madyar” Brovdi reported that drone detachments under his command accounted for 16,796 Russian military casualties in October – nearly 31 percent of the total 54,400 personnel losses confirmed by the president .
Over the course of the month, USF units struck 64,807 adversary targets across 255,605 combat missions, neutralizing a Russian serviceman every 159 seconds on average.
Roughly 69.5 percent of drone-inflicted Russian casualties occurred along the Dobropillia-Pokrovsk, Oleksandrivka, and Huliaipole operational axes, where loitering munitions, thermal-equipped bomber drones, and first-person view (FPV) strike craft disrupted enemy staging areas and armored columns before assault teams reached forward contact lines.
The record monthly losses in personnel and equipment compound cumulative assessments tracking the exhaustion of Russia’s conventional force generation.
A statistical study by The Economist calculated that total Russian casualties since February 2022 range between 1.4 million and 2.1 million killed and wounded , with battlefield fatalities reaching between 374,000 and 770,000.
The publication noted that the sharp escalation in fatal casualties over recent months reflects the increasing reliance of Russian field commands on frontal infantry charges to compensate for armor shortfalls.
The mounting losses have severely strained Russian domestic labor reserves, prompting Moscow to deploy thousands of North Korean troops in frontline combat while utilizing illicit overseas networks to bring North Korean forced laborers into Russian defense factories on fraudulent student visas, according to recent human rights investigations by Global Rights Compliance.
Concurrently, Ukrainian forces have coupled frontline resistance with precision interdiction against Russian military-industrial supply chains and energy hubs.
Over the final days of October, Ukrainian precision strikes destroyed an S-400 Triumf command post and a Pantsir-S2 complex valued at $70 million alongside the Kamensky solid rocket fuel plant in Rostov region, while long-range drones struck major oil processing refineries in Kstovo, Ufa, and Novokuybyshevsk.

articles.title_orig: 'They can't afford to keep the ones that they have': Jake and Spike clash over Seattle's $22 minimum wage
articles.title_zh: 'They can't afford to keep the ones that they have': Jake and Spike clash over Seattle's $22 minimum wage
articles.content_orig:
BY JAKE SKORHEIM AND SPIKE O'NEILL SHOW
The Jake and Spike Show, weekdays from 12 p.m. - 3 p.m.
KIRO host Jake Skorheim argued the problem facing Seattle small businesses isn’t finding workers.
“It’s not because they can’t find the employees,” Jake said on “The Jake and Spike Show” on KIRO Newsradio. “They can’t afford to keep the ones that they have.”
Seattle’s minimum wage will rise from $21.30 to $22.14 an hour on Jan. 1, 2027, according to the Seattle Office of Labor Standards . The increase is tied to inflation and applies to all employers, no matter how big or small. The statewide minimum wage will be $17.73 an hour in 2027.
The debate comes after a business climate survey from the Seattle Metro Chamber and the Downtown Seattle Association found 47% of business owners have “seriously considered” moving operations, jobs, or investment out of Seattle in the past year. Respondents pointed to public safety, taxes and fees, and labor costs as the reasons.
The argument started with how Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson answered a question about what she’s doing for small business owners. KIRO host Spike O’Neill described her as essentially reframing the question around workers.
“What she’s saying essentially is, ‘I’m going to make sure that you have a workforce that can afford to live and work for you,'” Spike said, paraphrasing the mayor. “That you don’t find a drought of potential employees because nobody can afford to live in the city.”
Jake countered that’s not what business owners are telling anyone.
“Because the costs are too expensive, because the city requires a minimum wage that is more than that person’s work,” Jake responded.
Spike wasn’t disagreeing. He was explaining the mayor’s position, noting that she’s responsible for more than just business owners.
“She’s also got responsibility to the citizens of Seattle who want to earn a living, that they can work and live in Seattle,” Spike said. “She’s got to serve two masters in this.”
“What she needs to serve is the overall public good,” Jake countered. “Is the overall public good going to be better when you have no businesses to employ the low-wage workers that she says need $22-plus an hour?”
Spike flipped the question back on him.
“Is the overall business of a city going to be better served if no one can afford to live here?” Spike asked.
Jake insisted the companies that are struggling aren’t the ones posting help-wanted signs.
“The reason those 47% of the businesses are thinking about relocating, leaving Seattle or driving across the bridge into Bellevue, it’s not because they can’t find the employees,” Jake said.
At least one downtown owner said much the same. Jamila Conley, who owns WeRise Wine Bar, told KIRO 7 she understands the appeal of moving east.
“You travel five miles over the water and your minimum wage drops, your insurance drops, your taxes drop,” Conley said. “I am Seattle ride or die, but it sure does look appealing.”
Considering a move isn’t the same as making one, though. Only 9% of business owners who answered that question said they expect to relocate outside Seattle in the next 12 months, according to the survey.
Jake then turned the question to Spike’s own life.
“Can you afford to live in Seattle?” Jake asked.
“No,” Spike responded. “I chose not to. I chose to have more space for what my dollar would get me. My dollar goes further out in the county.”
To Jake, that proved his point.
“All of your life is a little bit more affordable out there,” Jake said. “And you’ve made the choice to live out there.”

articles.title_orig: Poland’s fight over its constitutional court gets physical
articles.title_zh: Poland’s fight over its constitutional court gets physical
articles.content_orig:
Poland is in the throes of a constitutional crisis as a battle over the future of the country’s highest court ignites another confrontation between the country’s president and prime minister.
The crisis came to a head on Friday when center-left Prime Minister Donald Tusk moved to remake Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal, whose chief justice was appointed by the previous government – the far-right Law and Justice party (PiS).
The judge, Bogdan Święczkowski, was suspended after refusing to allow a new member of the Tribunal, who had been nominated by Tusk and approved by the Polish parliament, from taking his seat. His deputy was also suspended.
The current crisis is the latest and possibly most serious chapter in a long-running dispute over the rule of law in Poland.
Tusk’s pro-European Civic Coalition was elected in 2023, after an election campaign in which he promised to restore the Tribunal’s independence. President Karol Nawrocki, who belongs to PiS, was elected separately last year. Poland’s president has little executive power but plays an important constitutional role.
Since then, deadlock has become crisis.
Nawrocki described Święczkowski’s removal as the chief judge as “a forcible takeover of a constitutional body.” On hearing the news, he abandoned a trip to Africa, ordered his aircraft to turn round and headed straight to the Tribunal.
Nawrocki is a vocal supporter of US President Donald Trump, who said in September: “I endorsed him, and now he’s president and he’s doing a fantastic job.” Nawrocki has suggested a new US military base in Poland will be called “Fort Trump”.
During its eight years in power – until 2023 - PiS appointed several judges to seats on the Tribunal already filled by the previous government.
In 2021, the European Union warned that PiS’ actions posed a “systemic risk to the rule of law in Poland” in undermining the Tribunal’s independence. The European Commission froze $137 billion in EU funding for Poland over concerns about the independence of Polish judges.
The PiS-appointed judges remained in place after Tusk was elected and have obstructed his efforts to nominate new judges. Nawrocki has refused to swear in three of six judges nominated by ‌parliament, ‌while Swieczkowski declined to seat the judges chosen by parliament.
Last week, the latest judge to be approved by parliament – Maciej Berek - was prevented from taking his seat amid scuffles outside the Tribunal in Warsaw.
On Saturday, riot police reinforced security measures around the court in central Warsaw.
Tusk, who has spent much of his time as Prime Minister trying to unstitch the PiS changes to the judiciary, said his government was seeking to restore the rule of law.
“This process is difficult, at times even painful, ‌and requires decisive action. There is no other way,” he said on X Saturday.
In a televised speech Tusk said that “shouting, lies, and brawling cannot be the source of law in Poland, and they never will be.”
He insisted the Tribunal “will function as it should. Also, independently of me and in line with the constitution.”
Analysts say the crisis deepened when parliament approved the nomination of Berek, a close ally of Tusk.
It “contradicts the government’s pledge to depoliticise the Tribunal,” wrote Alberto Allemano, a professor of law at the HEC Paris Business School.
“The Friday suspension of the Tribunal’s president and vice-president, ordered by one judge and accompanied by a police presence outside the building, is not in itself a “coup”: the stated aim is to restore a lawfully functioning court. But restoring the rule of law must itself be done lawfully,” Allemano wrote on X .
At the same time, “If the Polish government is trying to repair an institution captured under PiS, its opposition is striving to retain some control through illegal means,” he added.
The US ambassador to Poland Tom Rose warned on Friday night that “thousands gathering outside the tribunal make an already dangerous situation more combustible. The last thing Poland needs is a confrontation that spirals into something far worse.”
“I hope everyone involved—government officials, law enforcement, and demonstrators alike, to take a deep breath, and don’t take any action that could provoke violence or further escalation,” Rose said on X.
But it’s unclear how the standoff between Tusk and Nawrocki can be resolved. Neither seems ready to compromise at a time when Poland faces growing security threats – with the war across the border in Ukraine, and sabotage attacks inside Poland that Tusk has attributed to Russia.
Tusk said Saturday of his opponents that it was “no coincidence that they find support among pro-Russian forces around the world.”
Fresh elections are due next year, with Poland’s constitutional order and its political direction – towards or away from deeper integration with Europe – high on the agenda.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft AI beats doctors in simulated diagnosis test
articles.title_zh: Microsoft AI beats doctors in simulated diagnosis test
articles.content_orig:
Laura Ingraham examines the impact of artificial intelligence on healthcare, questioning whether AI will replace doctors. A major public hospital system CEO plans to replace radiologists with AI for breast cancer screening, aiming for cost savings. Dr. Marc Siegel, Fox News Senior Medical Analyst, advocates for AI as a tool to enhance, not replace, human doctors, stressing the irreplaceable value of personal interaction and physician oversight for diagnoses.
Ever leave a doctor's appointment with more questions than answers? Maybe you've gone through several tests, only to hear that your doctor still isn't sure what's causing your symptoms. That uncertainty can be exhausting, especially when you want answers. Now, Microsoft says its new artificial intelligence system could help doctors solve some of medicine's toughest diagnostic puzzles. And the early numbers are impressive.
In a study published on Oct. 22 in the journal Science, Microsoft's AI diagnostic system correctly identified 83% of complex medical cases, compared with 36% for generalist physicians who could consult reference materials. That's more than twice the accuracy under the study's testing conditions.
However, there's an important catch behind those numbers. The research took place in a simulation, and the doctors weren't specialists working together on difficult cases. Still, the findings raise a fascinating question about how artificial intelligence could change your next visit to the doctor.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
AI MAY SPOT DEADLY HEART RISK IN A ROUTINE ECG
Microsoft's MAI-DxO system uses multiple AI agents to evaluate symptoms, recommend tests and work toward a diagnosis. (Microsoft AI)
Microsoft calls its technology the MAI Diagnostic Orchestrator, or MAI-DxO. The system uses multiple AI agents that work together much like a panel of doctors discussing a difficult medical case. Instead of jumping to an immediate answer, the AI begins with limited information. It asks follow-up questions and considers which medical tests might help identify the problem. Then, its AI agents challenge one another's conclusions as new information becomes available.
Think about someone who has unexplained fatigue and several unusual lab results. A doctor might consider one possible explanation before ordering additional tests. Microsoft's system can examine multiple possibilities and reconsider its initial assessment as the evidence changes. That approach could prove especially useful when symptoms overlap across different diseases.
According to Microsoft's published findings, researchers evaluated the technology using 304 complex medical cases from The New England Journal of Medicine . These cases often involve unusual illnesses that challenge even experienced physicians. The results were striking. MAI-DxO correctly diagnosed approximately 83% of those cases. Generalist physicians working alone achieved 36% accuracy when they could use reference materials. Without those resources, their accuracy dropped to 22%. Researchers also tested the system using historical emergency department cases. There, the AI achieved approximately 80% accuracy, compared with 47% for the physician comparison group.
Before anyone starts canceling doctor appointments, there's something important to understand about this research. The physicians in the comparison were generalists, including primary care doctors and general internists. They evaluated cases individually, even when they had access to medical reference materials.
However, hospitals typically involve specialists when patients develop particularly difficult medical problems. Those specialists may work together and review additional evidence before reaching a diagnosis. Microsoft did not directly compare its system against teams of medical specialists.
There's another important detail. Microsoft's AI was evaluated across 304 complex cases, while physicians worked through a smaller set of 56 cases held out from the system's development process. That means the headline percentages don't represent two groups completing exactly the same number of cases.
That limits how broadly we can interpret the findings. The researchers also relied on existing medical cases rather than treating patients in real time. While those cases provide a useful challenge, actual medical care can be far more unpredictable.
Patients sometimes struggle to describe symptoms. Medical records may contain gaps, and physical examinations can reveal clues that never appear in a written case summary. The simulation also relied on an AI system to supply information from existing case reports. When certain details weren't available, it could generate plausible responses. That helped researchers create diagnostic conversations, although those interactions cannot fully reproduce the uncertainty doctors encounter with actual patients.
Furthermore, reaching the correct diagnosis represents only part of caring for someone. Doctors must determine the appropriate treatment and understand how individual circumstances affect medical decisions. The study's authors also work for Microsoft, making independent testing especially important before hospitals consider relying on the technology for patient care. For now, Microsoft's results show how well the technology performed under controlled testing conditions. Whether it can deliver similar benefits during everyday patient care remains an open question.
HIDDEN CLUES COULD HELP PREDICT A WOMAN’S BREAST CANCER RISK YEARS IN ADVANCE
Microsoft's research suggests AI could eventually help doctors diagnose difficult medical conditions more accurately while keeping patients involved in their care. (iStock)
You might be wondering how this technology compares with ChatGPT or other AI assistants that already answer medical questions. The underlying AI models play a major role in Microsoft's system. In fact, the researchers tested models developed by OpenAI, Google , Anthropic and other companies.
One finding deserves attention. OpenAI's GPT-5 correctly solved approximately 79% of the complex cases when researchers used a basic prompt without Microsoft's orchestration system. Adding MAI-DxO increased accuracy to approximately 83%. That's an improvement, although the underlying AI model already performed remarkably well.
With the newer GPT-5.5 model, the gains were larger on complex cases. Microsoft's orchestration system raised accuracy from approximately 72% to nearly 87% in that comparison. However, the additional system provided little improvement on emergency department cases using the strongest models. These results suggest that much of the diagnostic capability comes from powerful AI models themselves. Microsoft's approach can improve its performance further, depending on the model and medical problem.
Meanwhile, Microsoft CEO of AI Mustafa Suleyman has described the company's larger ambition as "medical superintelligence." The idea involves developing AI systems capable of eventually exceeding today's strongest medical teams in clinical reasoning and coordination. Microsoft is also collaborating with Mayo Clinic on AI technology that could eventually help clinicians anticipate how a patient's medical condition might develop. Those ambitions extend well beyond the capabilities demonstrated in the current study.
